boundary: The Rocq capstones and the bounded TLA+ invariants specify the derived index; the named tests check a test-only reference oracle over real HotStore and RSpace instances, and the production witnesses check the production receive accelerator of task 8011 against the same obligations. Harness controls RAC-RS-01 to RAC-RS-16 and RAC-RS-25 show that each named test observes its property, and production controls RAC-RS-17 to RAC-RS-24 show that the tests observe the production revision signals. Production accelerator controls from RAC-RS-26 on fault the production accelerator and are killed by its production witnesses. None of this is a formal Rust refinement proof.
scope: Generation-bound receive occurrence index: the receive relation derived from the semantic roots and the versioned installed input, exact receive identifiers, revision-bound accelerator classes, artifact publication, failure atomicity and candidate commit (designs 8010 and 8011)

obligations.description: a receive identifier resolves by its hash bucket alone
a receive identifier is the record's ordinal in its group, so a maintained removal deletes the catalog entry at ordinal 0 instead of the named target
an absent accelerator answers the empty set
a stale accelerator answers from its old entries
the classifier ignores the generation, so an accelerator of a foreign generation is taken for a current or stale one
an incomplete accelerator is classified as coherent and answers
a repeated channel keeps only its first position
the observation records an installed receive as resting, so it shares one target with a byte-identical resting record
the derivation keeps only the first receive of each group's ordered lookup, so it depends on construction order
the automaton artifact keeps the previous revision
a failed update publishes its partially updated catalog while the accelerator stays marked current
the accelerator's occurrences carry a target that differs from the derived one, so the receive identity depends on whether the accelerator answered
an alias insertion replaces the first source
a candidate commits without the revision check
the target identity is the continuation body, which erases the persist flag and peeks
a removal leaves its occurrences in a current accelerator
put_continuation keeps the group's epoch after an insertion
install_continuation keeps the group's epoch
remove_continuation keeps the group's epoch
an accepted ordinary removal keeps the group's epoch
clear keeps the generation
set_state copies the old base epoch into its replacement
the stale-ticket check accepts a changed version
the retained-set automaton cache ignores the version
adoption ignores the bound semantic manifest
resolve accepts a target of equal identity length (production analogue of RAC-RS-01)
a removal of the first ordered record is treated as final and clears the published group (production analogue of RAC-RS-02)
an absent accelerator answers the exact empty set (production analogue of RAC-RS-03)
handle classification ignores the store revision, so a stale handle answers from its old index (production analogue of RAC-RS-04)
handle classification ignores the generation, so a handle of a foreign generation is taken for a current or stale one (production analogue of RAC-RS-05)
join groups outside the handle's loaded scope are skipped, so an unloaded join group leaves the channel answering (production analogue of RAC-RS-06)
an installed-only group outside the handle's loaded scope is skipped, so the channel answers without it (production analogue of RAC-CSMUT-02)
a channel whose joins are not loaded is treated as having no join groups, so it answers instead of falling back as incomplete (a production control with no harness analogue)
a repeated channel keeps only its first position (production analogue of RAC-RS-07)
an installed target is dropped beside a resting record with the same identity and source bytes (production analogue of RAC-RS-08)
